packageRules.description: vitest 5 drops Node 20 from its type peer: vitest 4.1.11 peerOptional-requires `@types/node ^20.0.0 || ^22.0.0 || >=24.0.0`, vitest 5.0.0 requires `^22.0.0 || >=24.0.0`. This repo pins `@types/node ^20.14.0` to track its engines floor, so npm cannot resolve and the pull request can never go green. Raising the pin to ^20.19.0 does not help: that satisfies vite 8, which is the conflict npm prints first, but not vitest 5 itself, which is the one that actually blocks. The only pin vitest 5 accepts is ^22 or >=24, and that means raising the engines floor off Node 20 first. Lift this together with engines.node and @types/node, not on its own.

Pin both `FROM` lines of the Dockerfile to the digest of their tag (`node:22-bookworm-slim@sha256:...`). A Docker Hub tag is mutable, so on a bare tag a rebuild of the same commit could ship a different base, and no commit recorded which base an image was built on. With the digest pinned, a new base arrives as a digest update inside the shared preset's `before 3am on Monday` (UTC) window, in its patches group, and the preset merges it on green CI. That CI does not build the image: .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml builds it on a version tag only, so a new base is first built with the next release. Apart from the two packages the Dockerfile upgrades by name, the base is the only way a Debian fix reaches the image, so a base fix can wait up to a week for the window, and then for a release. Scoped to the `dockerfile` manager: the shared preset pins digests for GitHub Actions only, and the `:latest` in examples/docker-compose.yml is meant to follow the newest release.
